chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdallah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Hanifan Musliman.' He said: Sincere and devoted, having in it nothing whatsoever of the worship of idols.

key_terms.حَنِيفًا: A Hanif, one who turns away from idolatry to pure monotheism
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: Muslim, one who submits completely to God

ai.seo_question: What does the term Hanifan Musliman mean in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the Quranic epithet 'Hanifan Musliman' applied to Prophet Ibrahim by defining it as a state of pure, exclusive monotheism (Tawhid) completely devoid of idolatry (Shirk). This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on *Ikhlas* (sincerity) as the core essence of submission to God, distinguishing true faith from mere ritualistic adherence mixed with polytheistic practices.
